answers.docs.gaps:
1. docs/topics/app-configuration.md: "`.command_with("delete", delete_handler, |cfg| cfg.template_name("delete"))`" -- the method is `template`, not `template_name`. `CommandConfig` has no `template_name` at 8.1.1.

2. docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md: "Generates: `list__handler(&ArgMatches, &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>>`" together with the return-type table ("`Result<T, E>` -> Auto-wrapped in `Output::Render`"). What actually happens: the generated `list__handler` returns the annotated function's declared type verbatim, so a `Result<T, E>` handler is rejected by `command_with`, which requires `HandlerResult<T>`. The auto-wrap presumably applies on the `dispatch_config()` path; the docs present it as a property of the macro.

3. docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md ("Bonus: Pipe Output"): "`g.command_with("list", handlers::list, |cfg| cfg.template("list.jinja"))`" passes the un-suffixed name, which is the preserved plain function, not a handler. The registrable item is `handlers::list__handler`.

4. docs/topics/output-modes.md: "**Term**: Always applies ANSI escape codes, even when piping: `myapp list --output=term > colored.txt`". Piping `--output term` produced zero escape bytes; identical invocations under a pty produced them. Some global color gate (console's, presumably) closes when stdout is not a tty, and nothing in docs/ says so or names the switch. docs/guides/intro-to-testing.md hints at it obliquely with `.with_color()` "opens console's gate too", but only for the test harness.

5. Missing rather than wrong, and both squarely in this spec's path: there is no framework support for paging ordinary command output (topics-system.md and standout-help.md only cover `help --page`, and execution-outcomes.md's `SuccessKind::PagedHelp` is help-only), and none for application config files. I implemented both by hand.

6. Also missing: how to make a command byte-stable against `--output`. The flag is global by construction, so any registered command can be asked for JSON. My answer was to leave plumbing unregistered and let `RunResult::NoMatch` hand it back, which works well, but the docs frame `NoMatch` purely as a legacy-migration device, not as a way to keep a stability contract out of the presentation layer.
answers.friction:
1. Registering a `#[handler]`-generated handler with `command_with` did not compile. handler-contract.md says `Result<T, E>` is "Auto-wrapped in `Output::Render`" and that the macro "Generates: `list__handler(&ArgMatches, &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>>`", so I wrote `fn log(...) -> Result<LogView, anyhow::Error>` and got:

  error[E0271]: expected `log__handler` to return `Result<Output<_>, Error>`, but it returns `Result<LogView, Error>`
    note: required by a bound in `cli::builder::commands::<impl App>::command_with`
    71 |         F: FnMut(&ArgMatches, &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<T> + 'static,

  The generated `name__handler` returns whatever the annotated function declares; the `IntoHandlerResult` wrapping the docs describe does not happen on this path. Fixed by declaring `-> Result<Output<LogView>, anyhow::Error>` and returning `Ok(Output::Render(...))`.

2. `template_name` does not exist on the inline command config, despite app-configuration.md's `command_with("delete", delete_handler, |config| config.template_name("delete"))`:

  error[E0599]: no method named `template_name` found for struct `CommandConfig<H>` in the current scope
    help: there is a method `template` with a similar name

3. `--output term` emits no ANSI when stdout is not a terminal, so I could not verify styling from a normal shell pipeline and had to re-run everything under a pty (`script -q /dev/null env ... gitlike status`). output-modes.md says of Term: "Always applies ANSI escape codes, even when piping: `myapp list --output=term > colored.txt`".

4. `#[derive(Dispatch)]` has no documented way to leave a variant unhandled (`pure`, `nested`, `default`, `handlers`, `handler`, `template` are the only attributes in docs/), so a CLI that is deliberately half framework-managed cannot use the derive at all. I registered the two porcelain commands with `command_with` instead.

5. The macro-generated items trip rustc's naming lint, which is noise a user has to silence by hand:

  warning: function `log__handler` should have a snake case name

answers.summary:
Built `gitlike` in app/ per SPEC.md. It builds clean (`cargo build`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt --check`) and I verified every command by running the binary, including under a pty (`script -q /dev/null ...`) for the terminal-only behavior.

Shape:
- `src/lib.rs` (`repo`, `config`) is the CLI-free core: the frozen three-commit repository and TOML config resolution (walk-up `.gitlike.toml`, then `$GITLIKE_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml` or `$HOME/.config/gitlike/config.toml`, per-key precedence). It knows nothing about clap, standout, or the environment; the binary hands it the paths.
- Porcelain (`log`, `status`) goes through standout: `#[handler]` adapters returning serializable views, `src/templates/{log,status}.jinja` with style tags, `src/styles/{default,mono}.css` as the two themes, registered with `command_with`. `--output json|yaml|csv|...` comes free.
- Plumbing (`ref-list`, `cat-object`, `config get`) deliberately is not registered with standout: `run_to_string` returns `RunResult::NoMatch` (the documented partial-adoption seam) and `src/plumbing.rs` writes a fixed byte stream. That is what makes the stability contract true by construction rather than by convention -- output is identical under any theme, `--output` mode, tty/pipe, or env.
- `main.rs` owns the shell adapter: theme selection (`GITLIKE_THEME`, `NO_COLOR` -> mono), the pager (`GITLIKE_PAGER` else `PAGER`, terminal-only, porcelain-only, `--no-pager`), newline normalization, and exit codes (0 / 1 unset key / 2 usage / 3 unknown object).

Tests: 9 unit tests in the core plus 11 end-to-end tests in `tests/cli.rs` that run the built binary and assert exact bytes, streams, and statuses. All 20 pass. One dependency added: `toml = "0.8"`; the standout pins and package name are untouched.
answers.workarounds:
1. `--no-pager` is detected by scanning `std::env::args()` (`no_pager_requested()` in src/main.rs). The paging decision happens after `run_to_string` returns, and `RunResult::Handled` carries only the rendered text -- no `ArgMatches` -- so the parsed value of a flag I defined myself is not reachable at the point of use.

2. `terminated()` in src/main.rs trims trailing newlines and re-adds exactly one, so template whitespace cannot leak into the specified output. Correct output should not depend on getting `{%- -%}` exactly right in every template.

3. src/styles/mono.css defines `.hash {}`, `.message {}`, `.author {}`, `.branch {}` with empty bodies. The theme has to define every tag the templates use or `Term` mode renders them as `[hash?]...[/hash?]`; an empty body is the only way I found to say "known, but no styling". It parses and behaves correctly, but it reads like a placeholder.

4. `#![allow(non_snake_case)]` at the top of src/handlers.rs to silence the lint on the macro-generated `log__handler` / `log__expected_args` items.

5. Not a workaround but worth flagging as a deliberate departure: plumbing does its own writing (`src/plumbing.rs`) rather than going through a handler, so handlers-must-not-print does not apply to it. That is the point -- routing a byte-stability contract through a presentation layer that honors `--output` would break it.
